title: Relief and Righteous Judgment When Jesus Comes
summary_text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy thank God for the Thessalonians' growing faith, love, and endurance under persecution. Their suffering for the kingdom of God shows His righteous judgment: He will give the oppressed relief and repay their oppressors. When Jesus Christ appears with angels in fire, those who reject God and His gospel face eternal destruction away from the Lord's presence and glory. Jesus will be glorified among His saints, who marvel at Him. The writers pray that God's power will fulfill the believers' work of faith, so Jesus is glorified in them through grace.
key_points: The writers thank God for increasing faith and love and praise the believers' endurance through persecution.
God's righteous judgment brings relief to those suffering for His kingdom and affliction to their oppressors.
Jesus' fiery appearing brings eternal destruction to those rejecting the gospel and wonder among His saints.
The writers pray for lives worthy of God's calling, with Jesus glorified in the believers through grace.

title: Lawlessness Must Appear Before the Lord's Day
summary_text: Paul warns against claims that the Day of the Lord has already arrived, saying rebellion and the man of lawlessness must appear first. This man will claim to be God in God's temple, but a restrainer still holds him back. Satan will empower his deceptive signs, yet Jesus will destroy him at His coming. Those who reject truth and delight in wickedness receive delusion from God and face judgment. Paul thanks God for choosing the believers for salvation through the Spirit's sanctification and faith in truth, calls them to hold to his teaching, and prays for strength and hope through grace.
key_points: Paul denies that the Lord's day has come and says rebellion and the man of lawlessness must appear first.
A restrainer holds lawlessness back until its proper time, and Jesus will destroy the lawless one when He appears.
Satan's deception meets willing rejection of truth, and God sends delusion leading to judgment.
God chose them for salvation through the Spirit's sanctification and faith, calling them through the gospel to Christ's glory.
Paul urges them to hold firmly to his teaching and prays for comfort and strength from Christ and the Father.

title: Prayer and Work While Doing Good
summary_text: Paul asks for prayer that the Lord's word will spread and that the missionaries will escape wicked people, while assuring believers that the Lord is faithful to guard them. He commands them in Christ's name to keep away from those who refuse an orderly life, recalling how he worked to support himself. Those unwilling to work must not eat; Paul tells them to earn their own food instead of interfering in others' affairs. The church must keep doing good and correct disobedient members as brothers rather than enemies. Paul closes with a prayer for peace, his handwritten greeting, and grace.
key_points: Paul seeks prayer for the Lord's word to spread and trusts the faithful Lord to protect the believers.
The missionaries worked to support themselves, offering an example instead of burdening the church.
Paul commands those unwilling to work to stop meddling and earn their living quietly.
Believers must continue doing good and warn the disobedient as brothers, even while withdrawing from them.
Paul prays for peace and adds his handwritten greeting as the identifying mark of his letters.
